sections.title: Cache setup and reading saved data
sections.what: Creates the cache with a folder and a time limit, and reads saved data. It returns the data when the file exists and is recent, and nothing otherwise.
sections.why: Likely reason: checking age on read stops old research from being reused.
sections.watch_out: The age check uses the computer's clock, so a clock change can make entries look too old or too new.

sections.name: ResearchCache: set
sections.title: Saving and clearing cache entries
sections.what: Saves data with the current time into a file named after the key, and deletes either one saved item or all of them.
sections.why: Likely reason: storing the time next to the data is what lets reading decide whether it has expired.
sections.watch_out: A failed save only writes a log message, so the caller gets no sign and may assume the data was stored.

summary: Stores research results as JSON files on disk for a set time, so the same lookup does not have to fetch the web again.
purpose: Makes the app faster and reduces repeated requests to research sites.
why: Likely reason: research sites are slow and may limit requests, so results are kept for one day by default.
how: 1. When created, makes sure the cache folder exists. 2. To save, writes the data and the current time into a file named after the key. 3. To read, opens the file, checks its age against the time limit, and returns the data or nothing. 4. To clear, deletes one file or every JSON file in the folder.
inputs: A cache folder path, a time limit in seconds (default 86400, one day), a key name, and data to save.
outputs: The saved data, or nothing if it is missing, expired or unreadable. Log messages.
risks: The key is used directly as a file name with no check, so a key containing folder symbols could write outside the cache folder. Save errors are logged but not raised, so the caller may think the save worked. Clearing everything deletes all JSON files in the folder. Expiry uses the computer's clock.
debug: If results never appear, check the log for cache hit, expired or error messages. If old data keeps coming back, check the time limit and the timestamp in the file. Delete the file for a key to reset it.
